quickSummary: Meiosis II is an equational division separating sister chromatids. In Metaphase II, chromosomes align on a single plate. In Anaphase II, centromeres split simultaneously, separating sister chromatids into individual daughter chromosomes. Telophase II and Cytokinesis II yield 4 genetically unique haploid gamete cells (n, C). Mitosis yields 2 identical diploid cells (2n); Meiosis I halves ploidy (2n -> n); Meiosis II halves DNA mass (2C -> C).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
MEIOSIS II STAGES
                                   │
  Prophase II ──► Metaphase II ──► Anaphase II ──► Telophase II
  (Nuclear        (Single Plate)   (**Centromeres  (Yields 4
  Breakdown)                       SPLIT**)        Haploid Cells)
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Prophase II**: Nuclear envelope breaks down again, chromosomes recondense.
• **Metaphase II**: Chromosomes align along a **single equatorial plate** in each dyad cell.
• **Anaphase II**: **Centromeres split simultaneously**; sister chromatids separate into daughter chromosomes migrating toward opposite poles ($n, 2C \rightarrow n, C$).
• **Telophase II & Cytokinesis II**: Nuclear envelopes reform around the four haploid chromosome sets, yielding **4 genetically non-identical haploid cells ($n, C$)**.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 5.1 Mitosis vs. Meiosis I vs. Meiosis II Comparison Matrix
conceptBreakdown.title: 5.1 Mitosis vs. Meiosis I vs. Meiosis II Comparison Matrix
conceptBreakdown.content:
| Feature | Mitosis | Meiosis I | Meiosis II |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Division Type** | **Equational** ($2n \rightarrow 2n$) | **Reductional** ($2n \rightarrow n$) | **Equational** ($n \rightarrow n$) |
| **Synapsis & Bivalents** | **ABSENT** | **PRESENT** (Zygotene) | **ABSENT** |
| **Crossing Over** | **ABSENT** | **PRESENT** (Pachytene) | **ABSENT** |
| **Metaphase Plate** | Single metaphase plate | **Double metaphase plate** | Single metaphase plate |
| **Anaphase Action** | Centromeres split; sister chromatids separate | **Homologous chromosomes separate**; centromeres do NOT split | Centromeres split; sister chromatids separate |
| **Daughter Cell Count** | 2 Genetically identical cells | 2 Haploid cells ($n, 2C$) | **4 Genetically unique haploid cells ($n, C$)** |
